english.note: Use this as the all-purpose colloquial verb for enjoying or favoring something, including mild romantic interest in a person.
Use this as the everyday choice for liking someone or something, including the emphatic sense of really liking it.
Use this colloquial choice when “enjoy” means generally liking an activity or finding it pleasurable.
Use this when “rate” means to like or approve of something rather than assess it formally.

examples.english: I like drinking iced lemon tea.
examples.jyutping: ngo5 zung1 ji3 jam2 dung3 ling4 caa4

examples.english: I really love drinking Hong Kong-style milk tea.
examples.traditional: 我真係鍾意食港式奶茶。
examples.jyutping: ngo5 zan1 hai6 zung1 ji3 sik6 gong2 sik1 naai5 caa4

examples.english: I enjoy listening to music after work.
examples.jyutping: ngo5 zung1 ji3 fong3 gung1 hau6 teng1 go1
ngo5 gei2 zung1 ji3 ni1 sau2 go1

english.note: Use 鍾意 when fancying someone means being attracted to or liking them romantically, sexually, or aesthetically.

examples.traditional: 我真係鍾意咗嗰個男仔。
examples.jyutping: ngo5 zan1 hai6 zung1 ji3 zo2 go2 go3 naam4 zai2
